KEY MESSAGE 1...Rain is expected tonight into Monday afternoon.
Enough rain to make a small dent in the drought, mostly 
Downeast, is likely with some places getting over an inch of 
rain.

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...
Models are still trending toward a more southern track for low 
pressure later tonight into Monday. However, uncertainty with the 
track still exists. The southern envelope of model solutions would 
track the low center across the southern Gulf of Maine later tonight 
through early Monday, then exiting across Nova Scotia later Monday. 
The more northern envelop of solutions still track the low along the 
Downeast coast later tonight through early Monday then exiting 
across New Brunswick later Monday. Rain totals with this system will 
be dependent on the eventual track. The heaviest rain totals will 
likely occur along, and just north of, the eventual low track where 
a swath of 1 to 2 inches of rain is likely. Locally greater 
totals are possible. Whether these heavier totals remain across 
the Gulf of Maine or extend into the Downeast region remains 
uncertain. Rainfall totals should steadily diminish 
northwestward across central and northern portions of the 
forecast area. Current indications are that rain totals from 
west-central to northeast portions of the forecast area should 
fall below an inch. The least rain should occur across portions 
of the North Woods where rain totals will likely remain below a 
tenth of an inch. However, all of these rain totals will be 
dependent on the eventual low track. A last minute 
northward/southward change in the eventual track could result in
higher or lower rain totals. A few thunderstorms are also 
possible along the Downeast coast and Gulf of Maine in advance 
of the system dependent on the eventual track. This is a 
relatively fast moving system. Rain will expand across the 
region overnight, persist through Monday morning, then diminish 
during the afternoon with the low exiting across the Maritimes. 
With the recent dry conditions the only expected impacts from 
the rain are possible localized urban/poor drainage flooding. No
snow is expected with this system.

KEY MESSAGE 2...An active weather pattern is likely from late on
Thanksgiving into next weekend. Forecast confidence on any 
particular weather system is low, but travelers should continue 
to monitor this period for potential travel disruptions.

KEY MESSAGE 2 DESCRIPTION...
The general weather pattern from Thanksgiving through the 
weekend is favorable for active weather. This is important 
given the busy travel period. However, it is simply too early to
know with such significant uncertainty in the track, strength, 
and timing of the system.

Models are currently overall in agreement on a low developing
off the eastern coast of Florida late Wednesday and making its 
way up the east coast. Most models have decent precipitation 
during this period as well. Models are also in overall agreement
that this system won’t reach Maine until late Thursday 
night/Friday morning. The issue is currently whether or not it 
may be too warm for snow. If the system is on the colder side, 
snow accumulation is possible, but it could just as easily be 
mostly rain for most of the area. Odds favor rain Downeast and 
tilt more toward snow in the far north. It is hard to get more 
specific than this as it is simply too early to know with such 
significant uncertainty at this time.

In summary, it is still too early to be overly alarmed or alter
travel plans, but be aware of the potential for active weather
that could impact travel Thanksgiving evening through Sunday, 
and continue to check back with us for updates.
